steps.phase: Read and bound the frozen brief
steps.title: Start from the live problem statement
steps.content:
Problem: Design an Autonomous Vehicle Perception System. Slug: design-an-autonomous-vehicle-perception-system. Description: Design the perception stack for an autonomous vehicle that fuses data from cameras, LiDAR, and radar sensors, detects objects in 3D space, and tracks their movement in real-time.

Requirements (verbatim):
- Process multi-camera feeds in real-time
- Process LiDAR point clouds for 3D detection
- Fuse sensor data for unified world model
- Detect and classify objects (vehicles, pedestrians, signs)
- Track object trajectories over time
- Estimate depth and distance accurately
- Handle adverse weather and lighting conditions
- Predict object motion for path planning

Constraints (verbatim):
- End-to-end perception latency under 100ms
- Object detection accuracy (mAP) above 90%
- Process 30+ frames per second
- Operate on edge hardware (automotive-grade GPUs)
- Handle 360-degree surround perception

Hints (verbatim):
- Use BEV (Bird's Eye View) representations for fusion
- Implement PointPillars or CenterPoint for LiDAR detection
- Use temporal fusion for multi-frame tracking
- Deploy with TensorRT optimization for edge inference
- Implement data-parallel training on multi-GPU clusters
- Use synthetic data generation for training augmentation

Companies listed: Waymo, Tesla, Cruise, NVIDIA. They are examples from the problem row, not required vendors. The live catalog row currently has has_guided_walkthrough=false. This file is a local review draft; it does not change that flag or establish publication.

steps.phase: Read and bound the frozen brief
steps.title: Keep unsupplied operating details open
steps.content: The brief gives no camera count or placement, sensor rates or formats, synchronization tolerance, calibration procedure, operating-condition set, depth-error tolerance, evaluation dataset, mAP aggregation method, or definition of the end-to-end latency boundary. Ask for these inputs before sizing or claiming that a design meets a target. Do not turn an example architecture into a measured guarantee.

steps.phase: Ingest and align the surround sensors
steps.title: Mark the camera, LiDAR, and radar input boundary
steps.content: The current palette has no dedicated camera, LiDAR, or radar sensor component, so use one generic custom node to mark these inputs. The node represents the modalities named by the brief; it does not assert sensor count, placement, or a particular interface.

component.label: Camera, LiDAR & Radar Inputs
component.description: Input boundary for the multi-camera feeds, LiDAR point clouds, and radar observations named in the problem.

properties.subtitle: No dedicated sensor component in the current palette
properties.purpose: Receive the camera, LiDAR, and radar data described by the frozen brief. Arrange the eventual camera and sensor coverage to satisfy the stated 360-degree surround requirement; sensor count, placement, formats, and rates remain unspecified.

component.highlightReason: The palette has no dedicated sensor-input types; this single custom node is limited to the three modalities explicitly named by the problem.

steps.phase: Ingest and align the surround sensors
steps.title: Prepare sensor observations for fusion
steps.content: Use the existing Processing Worker type for timestamp association, calibration transforms, and input preparation. The exact synchronization and calibration criteria must come from the selected sensors and the system validation plan; the problem supplies no tolerances.

component.label: Sensor Alignment & Preparation
component.description: Prepare camera, LiDAR, and radar observations for the perception path.

properties.purpose: Associate observations in time, apply the selected sensor calibration transforms, and prepare inputs for BEV fusion. Define tolerances from the actual sensor configuration; none are stated in the brief.

component.highlightReason: The unified world model depends on preparing the named sensor inputs for fusion, while the brief leaves synchronization and calibration details open.

steps.phase: Ingest and align the surround sensors
steps.title: Connect sensor inputs to preparation
steps.content: Keep all named modalities on the same preparation path so the fusion stage can form a unified view. Validate that the actual sensor arrangement covers the required surround field.

connection.label: Camera, LiDAR & radar observations
connection.description: Carry the sensor data named by the brief into time association, calibration, and input preparation; exact protocols and rates are not supplied.

steps.phase: Produce and serve 3D perception
steps.title: Place inference at the vehicle edge
steps.content: Use the palette's Edge Server as the local compute boundary. The purpose records the frozen automotive-grade GPU constraint; the palette does not provide a structured automotive GPU selection, so do not fill in a vendor or model.

component.label: Vehicle Edge Compute
component.description: Local edge boundary for the perception inference runtime.

properties.purpose: Host perception inference on the automotive-grade GPU edge hardware required by the brief. The specific GPU, memory budget, and vehicle compute configuration are not provided.

component.highlightReason: The stated deployment constraint places perception on automotive-grade GPU hardware at the vehicle edge.

steps.phase: Produce and serve 3D perception
steps.title: Add the edge inference serving boundary
steps.content: The existing Model Serving type represents the inference runtime. TensorRT appears in the frozen hints as an optimization to evaluate; the current serving-platform options do not include TensorRT, so keep it in the descriptive purpose instead of setting an unsupported platform value.

component.label: Edge Perception Inference Runtime
component.description: Serve the perception model locally on the vehicle edge.

properties.purpose: Run the perception model on the local automotive-grade GPU hardware. Evaluate the supplied TensorRT optimization hint against the selected model and target hardware; no serving platform or measured performance is specified by the brief.

component.highlightReason: This is the explicit edge inference boundary for the under-100ms end-to-end and 30+ frames-per-second constraints.

steps.phase: Produce and serve 3D perception
steps.title: Place the inference runtime on local hardware
steps.content: Treat the edge-to-serving link as the deployment relationship. Validate the complete request path on the selected automotive-grade GPU rather than inferring latency or throughput from this diagram.

connection.label: Hosts local inference
connection.description: The vehicle edge hardware hosts the serving runtime; the actual GPU and measured latency/frame rate remain to be established.

steps.phase: Produce and serve 3D perception
steps.title: Model BEV fusion and 3D object perception
steps.content: Use the supported Computer Vision model type for the perception model. Treat BEV as the supplied fusion hint, and evaluate PointPillars or CenterPoint as LiDAR detection candidates within the chosen sensor-fusion design. This does not claim that either candidate meets the target mAP or latency.

component.label: BEV 3D Perception Model
component.description: Fuse aligned sensor inputs and produce 3D object perception outputs.

properties.purpose: Use a BEV representation to fuse the prepared camera, LiDAR, and radar inputs. Detect and classify the named object categories in 3D and estimate depth and distance. Benchmark PointPillars or CenterPoint for LiDAR detection; no model, framework, or accuracy result is selected by the brief.

component.highlightReason: This model is the fusion and 3D detection boundary for object classes, depth, and distance.

steps.phase: Produce and serve 3D perception
steps.title: Send prepared observations to edge inference
steps.content: Carry the prepared multimodal observations into the local inference runtime. The under-100ms and 30+ frames-per-second targets apply to the full perception path and still need a precise measurement definition.

connection.label: Prepared sensor observations
connection.description: Forward time-associated and calibrated input for edge inference; the input representation and synchronization tolerances depend on the selected sensors.

steps.phase: Produce and serve 3D perception
steps.title: Invoke the BEV perception model
steps.content: Keep serving and model definition distinct: the runtime executes the perception model, while benchmark results determine whether the stated accuracy and end-to-end latency targets are met.

connection.label: Run perception inference
connection.description: The edge serving runtime invokes the BEV perception model and returns its 3D perception result.

steps.phase: Track motion into planning
steps.title: Track objects across frames and predict motion
steps.content: Use the supported Forecasting model type for the temporal trajectory and motion-prediction stage. The hint calls for temporal fusion; the tracking method, history window, and prediction horizon are not specified and must be selected and evaluated separately.

component.label: Temporal Tracking & Motion Prediction
component.description: Maintain object trajectories over time and estimate motion for path planning.

properties.purpose: Use detections across frames to track object trajectories and predict object motion for the downstream path-planning consumer. Apply temporal fusion as suggested by the problem hint; the method and prediction horizon remain open.

component.highlightReason: Temporal tracking and motion prediction cover the trajectory and path-planning requirements.

steps.phase: Track motion into planning
steps.title: Pass detections into temporal tracking
steps.content: Feed the 3D detections and classifications into temporal fusion so the design can maintain object trajectories over time.

connection.label: 3D detections across frames
connection.description: Provide model detections and their temporal observations to the tracking and motion-prediction stage.

steps.phase: Track motion into planning
steps.title: Mark the path-planning integration boundary
steps.content: Use the existing Backend Server type for the downstream path-planning consumer. It is an integration boundary only; this walkthrough does not design path planning or add behavior beyond the perception output named in the brief.

component.label: Path Planning Consumer (outside scope)
component.description: Downstream consumer of predicted object motion; path-planning internals are outside this problem's perception scope.

properties.purpose: Receive predicted object motion for path planning. The path planner's own requirements and interface are not specified by this problem.

component.highlightReason: The frozen brief explicitly names path planning as the consumer of predicted object motion.

steps.phase: Track motion into planning
steps.title: Connect predicted motion to path planning
steps.content: Expose the motion prediction result to the path-planning boundary while leaving the planner's internal behavior outside the design.

connection.label: Predicted object motion
connection.description: Deliver tracked trajectories and predicted object motion to the downstream consumer named by the problem.

steps.phase: Train and validate against the stated targets
steps.title: Represent the hinted training path
steps.content: Use the existing Model Training type and its supported Distributed compute value for the data-parallel, multi-GPU training hint. For reproducibility, retain references from each training run to the selected training-data revision (including synthetic-data inputs), code/configuration, and resulting candidate model. The brief does not prescribe provenance fields or storage; treat this as a design consideration, not an added requirement. Keep hardware, dataset composition, training schedule, and augmentation policy unspecified until selected from evidence.

component.label: Perception Model Training
component.description: Offline data-parallel training and synthetic-data augmentation path.

properties.purpose: Train the perception model with data-parallel work on a multi-GPU cluster and use synthetic data generation for training augmentation, as suggested by the problem hints. Include adverse weather and lighting cases in the selected augmentation/evaluation plan without claiming they guarantee robustness. Keep references to the selected data revision, synthetic-data inputs, code/configuration, and candidate model together for reproducibility; the brief specifies neither lineage fields nor storage. Define datasets, synthetic scenarios, hardware, and training configuration separately; the brief supplies no values for them.

component.highlightReason: This offline path reflects the problem's multi-GPU and synthetic-data training hints and supports evaluation under adverse weather and lighting.

steps.phase: Train and validate against the stated targets
steps.title: Measure the complete real-time path
steps.content: Validate the full path from sensor input through inference and tracking against end-to-end perception latency under 100ms and processing 30+ frames per second. Retain the measured results with the tested edge configuration and agreed measurement definitions so reviewers can see the evidence behind each claim. The brief does not say whether the frame-rate figure is aggregate or per stream, or define the latency clock boundary; agree those definitions and test on the target edge hardware. A diagram or model benchmark alone does not demonstrate either target.

steps.phase: Train and validate against the stated targets
steps.title: Define evidence for accuracy and operating coverage
steps.content: Evaluate object detection at the stated mAP above 90% and test the required 360-degree surround perception. Retain the evaluation-set revision, object-class and mAP aggregation protocol, operating conditions, and measured results with the candidate model as review evidence; the brief does not prescribe a report format or evidence store. It also leaves the evaluation set, object-class protocol, camera layout, and sensor overlap undefined. Measure depth and distance behavior and include adverse weather and lighting conditions in validation, but do not invent a numeric tolerance or claim coverage until those protocols are specified.

steps.phase: Train and validate against the stated targets
steps.title: Review the design against only the supplied contract
steps.content: The proposed graph covers camera, LiDAR, and radar input; sensor preparation; BEV 3D perception; temporal trajectories; edge inference; and predicted motion delivered to path planning. Training provenance and evaluation results should remain associated with the candidate so the evidence can be reviewed. The frozen brief does not define a registry, approval, release, or promotion lifecycle; this design ends at a candidate and its validation evidence, not an approved or deployed model. Obtain the missing sensor and evaluation definitions, then measure every frozen constraint on the target configuration. This draft adds no numerical specifications, vendor mandate, or claim that a target has been achieved.
